key_insight: A quantics tensor-train (QTT) Chebyshev–Galerkin method solves global spectral boundary-value problems directly in compressed form while preserving their variational structure.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables accurate elasticity analysis across large design and uncertainty spaces without explicitly storing every field coefficient.
method: Assemble weak-form spectral systems directly in QTT format without forming full arrays.
Handle coupled elliptic systems, variable coefficients, smooth geometry mappings, and mixed Dirichlet–Robin boundaries.
Treat parameters and random inputs as additional coordinates to solve entire parameter spaces at once.
evidence_signal: Reported results include errors below 10⁻⁸ on a 3D elasticity benchmark, 1.7×10⁷ cantilever designs solved in 92 seconds, and 2.4×10⁶-fold memory reduction for a problem with ten random coordinates.
watch_item: Efficiency depends on tensor compressibility; the reported benchmarks do not establish comparable gains for poorly compressible problems.
paper_title: A Tensor-Network Chebyshev-Galerkin Method for Boundary-Value Problems in Computational Mechanics
